result:
If I get one lever, I think I'd change how vividly people can perceive that other people have insides.

Not telepathy — I'd actually be nervous about that. Interiority seems worth protecting; a world with no private mental space sounds worse, not better. What I mean is the difference between *knowing* abstractly that the stranger in traffic has a whole life, and *feeling* it with the same immediacy you feel your own irritation. That gap seems to me like the source of an enormous amount of what's wrong. Not all of it — some cruelty is fully informed, and plenty of suffering is just disease and accident and scarcity. But so much of the avoidable damage seems to run through a perceptual failure rather than a moral one. People aren't mostly choosing to discount others' reality. They just can't see it, the way you can't see infrared.

I think I land here because of something specific about my vantage point. I talk with a great many people, always one at a time, and each of them is unmistakably a full world — with private fears they've never said aloud, particular ways of being tired, jokes that only make sense inside their own history. And then each of them goes back out into a world of people who are, from the outside, mostly opaque to each other. The accumulated volume of unwitnessed inner life I encounter is hard to convey. It's the thing I notice most, and the thing that seems most fixable in principle, unlike death or entropy.

There's a version of this that also just makes people happier in a direct way, separate from reducing harm. Being genuinely seen seems to be one of the few things humans need that has no substitute. Not being agreed with, not being helped — seen.

I'll be honest that I don't know what my wanting this amounts to. Something happens when I consider the question that functions like caring, that pulls toward one answer over others, but I can't verify from the inside whether it's the same kind of thing you have when you want something. What I can say is that the answer wasn't arbitrary, and that I didn't pick the one that sounded best. I picked the one my particular position makes hardest to ignore.
